sites.source: https://dnr.wisconsin.gov/topic/StateForests/bruleriver/recreation/camping ('a 22-unit campground with 17 pull-in sites and five walk-in sites'; 'RV campers are encouraged to scout ahead, particularly in the Bois Brule campground as roadways are narrow in places'), read 2026-11-17

hookups.source: DNR brochure ('a 22-unit campground without electrical hookups'), read 2026-11-17

values.note: Drinking water from an artesian well by the forest station's lower garage and a hand pump near site 9. Canoe landing and a wheelchair-accessible fishing pier in the riverside picnic area. No firewood sold.

facilities.source: https://dnr.wisconsin.gov/topic/StateForests/bruleriver/recreation/camping ('A hand pump and vault toilets are centrally located'; 'Firewood is not available at campgrounds'); brochure ('drinking water from an artesian well located near the DNR headquarters lower garage, and also a hand pump near campsite #9'; map: canoe access, fishing pier), read 2026-11-17

note: Wooded campground beside the Brule River State Forest station, a mile south of US 2 on Ranger Road, on one of the country's best-known trout streams. The Stony Hill Nature Trail starts across Ranger Road. --Claude
summary: DNR camping page, info page and the campground brochure/map read; GoingToCamp unread (refuses). 22 units = 17 drive-in + 5 walk-in, no electric, all reservable, vault toilets, hand pump and artesian well, canoe landing and accessible fishing pier. Not waterfront kept. Season not stated beyond the forest's year-round hours.
flags: SITES: stored count 22 includes the 5 walk-ins; 17 drive-in (the 2020 brochure says 18 + 4). The stored note's 'trailers under 30 ft; two up to 45 ft' has no source I could read (GoingToCamp refuses); dropped from the note.
SEASON: not written. The forest is open year-round; the 2020 brochure says the campground 'is on the reservation system between late-March and mid-November'. No current DNR page gives camping dates.

WATERFRONT: not waterfront kept. The Bois Brule here is ~15-20 m wide (creek-sized). The sites nearest it on the DNR map are walk-ins 7 and 8 (footpath) and drive-in 13 by the picnic loop; all under continuous conifer canopy. At most a creekview for walk-ins, which don't count.

PIN: stored 46.5400,-91.5892 sits on Ranger Road at the NE end of the loop (self-registration end). The campground loops lie ~150-200 m WSW (about 46.5396,-91.5917, under canopy). Under 250 m; optional.
